data.description:
## Context
The documentation system is strong, but several authoritative-looking entry points have drifted: README.md:39 and docs/user-guide.md:107 teach a bare --assignee alice although docs/config.md:416 says Jira reconciliation requires email/accountId; docs/README.md:87 describes removed .rebar/config.conf; docs/README.md:19 routes MCP use to the LLM framework instead of the generated MCP reference; optionality workflow comments describe dependency assumptions that no longer match pyproject.toml; mypy comments call non-core checking advisory even though CI gates the whole source tree.

## Plan
- Correct the affected examples and navigation labels against current configuration and CI contracts.
- Prefer omission of --assignee in quickstarts unless a clearly Jira-resolvable example is necessary.
- Update workflow/config comments so they explain current behavior rather than historical dependency topology.
- Extend an existing docs drift/golden check where a stable executable source of truth exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] README and user-guide assignee examples cannot teach a Jira-unresolvable bare handle.
- [ ] docs/README.md names rebar.toml/[tool.rebar] and routes MCP users to docs/mcp-reference.md.
- [ ] Optionality and mypy comments match current dependencies and blocking CI behavior.
- [ ] Relevant docs index/link/golden-path checks pass.
- [ ] At least one deterministic check protects a corrected high-risk truth from recurring drift.
data.title: Correct user-facing configuration, assignee, MCP, and optionality documentation drift
